label: VDA Depth
description: Video Depth Anything Large: temporally consistent relative depth for a frame range. Output: raw 32-bit EXR at plate size and plate frame numbers.
usage: Makes a depth pass for a frame range (Video Depth Anything Large).
Whole input range is sent; tick 'input range' to send only first-last. Desqueeze anamorphic plates first.
Result is relative inverse depth: white = near, black = far. It isn't metric.
0-1 is normalised over the frames sent, so two different ranges don't match each other. Render the whole shot in one go.
'input size' is the short side the model sees: higher = more detail, much more VRAM. Lower it first if you run out of memory.
highlights: what the model sees. 'clip' (default) cuts at 1 and keeps shadows open. 'roll off' compresses highlights but crushes deep shadows.
License (checked 2026-11): VDA Large weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0 - non-commercial only. Paid work needs another model, such as VDA Small (Apache-2.0).

output.tooltip: Depth is data, not colour: written and read as raw, in all three channels.

knobs.name: input_size
knobs.label: input size
knobs.tooltip: Short side the model sees (snapped to a multiple of 14). The result is scaled back to plate size. Plates wider than 16:9 get a smaller size automatically.

knobs.name: highlights
knobs.label: highlights
knobs.tooltip: What the model sees; only the input changes, as depth is data and isn't converted back. clip (default): values above 1 become 1 (colorimetric), shadows stay open. roll off: the plate goes in through ACES Output - sRGB, so highlights are compressed instead of cut, but deep shadows are crushed. Clip keeps shadow separation, which matters here because the node has an 8-bit step.

knobs.name: precision
knobs.label: precision
knobs.tooltip: fp32 uses more VRAM and runs slower.
